### Suite: bc (1 failures)

**Suite TL;DR:** The single bc-parallel failure is caused by a test-code regression in `createStoredEvent()` that changed the StoredEventValues map key from `v.DataType` ("notification"/"metric") to `v.Resource` (full ResourceAddress), silently dropping the LOCKED state so the test can never observe it.

**Root Cause Groups:**

- **Group 1: Test code key-scheme change in `createStoredEvent()` silently hides LOCKED state** (affects: `[It] [bc-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync`)
  - **Evidence:**
    ```
    [ptp.go: 411] got map[eventsource:/sync/sync-status/os-clock-sync-state
      eventtimestamp:2026-07-29 09:44:07.684026654 +0000 UTC
      eventtype:event.sync.sync-status.os-clock-sync-state-change
      eventvalues:map[/cluster/node/cnfdf30.telco5gran.eng.rdu2.redhat.com/CLOCK_REALTIME:-18]]
    [ptp.go: 419] clockOffset=0.000000
    [FAILED] OS Clock was never LOCKED and test timed out
    In [It] at: /tmp/cnf-pDNPW/ptp-operator-conformance-test/test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:393
    ```
    The raw cloud event data (logged by `event.go: 730`) clearly shows:
    ```json
    {"values":[
      {"ResourceAddress":"...CLOCK_REALTIME","data_type":"notification","value_type":"enumeration","value":"LOCKED"},
      {"ResourceAddress":"...CLOCK_REALTIME","data_type":"metric","value_type":"decimal64.3","value":"-18"}
    ]}
    ```
    The LOCKED event was delivered, but `values["notification"]` and `values["metric"]` were both `nil` in the test.

  - **Root Cause:** Commit `d20ffcbf` (PR #171, `CNF-19588`) changed `createStoredEvent()` in `test/pkg/event/event.go` (v1 path lines 711–717, v2 path lines 742–751) from using `v.DataType` as the map key to using `v.Resource` (the ResourceAddress). For `OsClockSyncState` events the notification value and metric value **share the same ResourceAddress** (`/cluster/node/.../CLOCK_REALTIME`), so the metric entry (`-18`) overwrites the notification entry (`LOCKED`) in the loop. The test at `ptp.go:414-415` then reads `values["notification"]` and `values["metric"]` — both return nil because those keys no longer exist — so `state` is `""` instead of `"LOCKED"`, `wasLocked` is never set `true`, and the test times out at `ptp.go:393`.

  - **Breaking PR/Commit:** Commit `d20ffcbf0cecd1cf94987788c703fa8d4565ba4d` — "CNF-19588: CI test for clockClass recovery after cloud-event-proxy crash" (merged as [PR #171](https://github.com/k8snetworkplumbingwg/ptp-operator/pull/171) on `main`). This is a `main`-only test code change; the `release-5.0` production images are unaffected. The OS clock on the hardware IS reaching LOCKED — the cloud event confirms it — but the test framework can't see it.

  - **Is it a flake?** No — the bug is deterministic. Every run will fail to observe LOCKED until the test times out.

  - **Suggested Fix:** In `test/pkg/event/event.go`'s `createStoredEvent()`, use a composite key `<ResourceAddress>:<DataType>` (or fall back to `DataType` when ResourceAddress is empty), so that OsClockSyncState events retain distinct "notification" and "metric" entries while BC clock class events with multiple "metric" values on different resources still don't collide. Alternatively, update `ptp.go:414-415` to iterate the values map and match by DataType rather than by fixed string keys.

**Suite Issue Class:** test_regression
**Suite Severity:** HIGH

**TL;DR:** Three independent `main`-branch regressions — a test key-scheme bug, a broken PMC invocation, and a T-BC topology mismatch — plus a ts2phc servo regression in the upstream sync caused all 36 failures.

## Root Cause Groups

- **2/36 failures — `createStoredEvent()` key-scheme change drops LOCKED state** (suites: bc, dualfollower)
  Commit `d20ffcbf` (PR #171, "CNF-19588") changed `test/pkg/event/event.go`'s `createStoredEvent()` to key the `StoredEventValues` map by `v.Resource` (ResourceAddress) instead of `v.DataType`. For `OsClockSyncState` events both the notification ("LOCKED") and metric ("-18") share the identical ResourceAddress, so the metric silently overwrites the notification in the loop. The test then reads `values["notification"]` and finds nothing, `wasLocked` is never set, and the test times out — even though the production cloud-event-proxy correctly delivered LOCKED.

- **21/36 failures — PMC command split + BC/HA clock stuck at FREERUN (clock class 248)** (suites: dualnicbc, dualnicbcha)
  Commit `14eb788` (PR #629, "Sync from upstream 22-Jul-2026" in `k8snetworkplumbingwg/linuxptp-daemon`) introduced a behavioral regression where pmc receives `GET` and `PARENT_DATA_SET` as two separate argv tokens instead of a single quoted string, returning `bad command: GET` / `bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET` for every PMC call. This prevents the test from reading `parentPortIdentity` or `grandmasterIdentity`, causing role-assertion failures (`ens2f0np0` stays in MASTER instead of SLAVE) and preventing clock class from ever reaching 6. All downstream clock-sync, outage-recovery, event-API, and metrics tests cascade from this single invocation bug.

- **2/36 failures — T-BC topology solver returns zero solutions** (suites: tbc, all)
  Commit `84723c83` (PR #205, "test: Add T-BC CI tests and configuration") added `PtpConfigTelcoBC()` and its `AlgoTelcoBCString="TBC"` constraint set to `test/pkg/testconfig/testconfig.go`, requiring a WPC NIC with receiver + two same-NIC transmitter ports and a co-located WPC GM. - **11/36 failures — WPC T-GM ts2phc servo stuck in FREERUN despite DPLL LOCKED** (suite: tgm)
  Also attributable to commit `14eb788` (PR #629 upstream sync). DPLL hardware on `cnfdf32` reports LOCKED (`dpll=1`) confirming valid GNSS/1PPS, but ts2phc software servo stays at FREERUN (`ts2phc=0`), indicating a regression in ts2phc log parsing, servo state-machine advancement, or GM clock-class propagation introduced by the sync (`log_parsing.go:82–153`, `ProcessTs2PhcEvents` in `daemon.go:2134–2190`). ### Suite: bc (1 failures)

**Suite TL;DR:** The single bc-parallel failure is caused by a test-code regression in `createStoredEvent()` that changed the StoredEventValues map key from `v.DataType` ("notification"/"metric") to `v.Resource` (full ResourceAddress), silently dropping the LOCKED state so the test can never observe it.

**Root Cause Groups:**

- **Group 1: Test code key-scheme change in `createStoredEvent()` silently hides LOCKED state** (affects: `[It] [bc-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync`)
  - **Evidence:**
    ```
    [ptp.go: 411] got map[eventsource:/sync/sync-status/os-clock-sync-state
      eventtimestamp:2026-07-29 09:44:07.684026654 +0000 UTC
      eventtype:event.sync.sync-status.os-clock-sync-state-change
      eventvalues:map[/cluster/node/cnfdf30.telco5gran.eng.rdu2.redhat.com/CLOCK_REALTIME:-18]]

    The raw cloud event data (logged by `event.go: 730`) clearly shows:

      {"ResourceAddress":"...CLOCK_REALTIME","data_type":"notification","value_type":"enumeration","value":"LOCKED"},
      {"ResourceAddress":"...CLOCK_REALTIME","data_type":"metric","value_type":"decimal64.3","value":"-18"}
    ]}
    ```
    The LOCKED event was delivered, but `values["notification"]` and `values["metric"]` were both `nil` in the test.

  - **Root Cause:** Commit `d20ffcbf` (PR #171, `CNF-19588`) changed `createStoredEvent()` in `test/pkg/event/event.go` (v1 path lines 711–717, v2 path lines 742–751) from using `v.DataType` as the map key to using `v.Resource` (the ResourceAddress). For `OsClockSyncState` events the notification value and metric value **share the same ResourceAddress** (`/cluster/node/.../CLOCK_REALTIME`), so the metric entry (`-18`) overwrites the notification entry (`LOCKED`) in the loop. The test at `ptp.go:414-415` then reads `values["notification"]` and `values["metric"]` — both return nil because those keys no longer exist — so `state` is `""` instead of `"LOCKED"`, `wasLocked` is never set `true`, and the test times out at `ptp.go:393`.

The OS clock on the hardware IS reaching LOCKED — the cloud event confirms it — but the test framework can't see it.

  - **Is it a flake?** No — the bug is deterministic. Every run will fail to observe LOCKED until the test times out.

  - **Suggested Fix:** In `test/pkg/event/event.go`'s `createStoredEvent()`, use a composite key `<ResourceAddress>:<DataType>` (or fall back to `DataType` when ResourceAddress is empty), so that OsClockSyncState events retain distinct "notification" and "metric" entries while BC clock class events with multiple "metric" values on different resources still don't collide. ### Suite: dualnicbc (11 failures)

**Suite TL;DR:** The dual-NIC boundary clock is stuck in FREERUN (clock class 248) and all PMC `GET PARENT_DATA_SET` queries return `bad command: GET / bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET`, cascading into clock-sync, event, outage-recovery, and metrics failures.

    bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET

    bad command: GET
    bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET
    ```
  - **Root Cause:** linuxptp's `pmc` binary processes each remaining argv entry as a separate command (e.g., `do_command("GET")` then `do_command("PARENT_DATA_SET")`), producing one "bad command" error per token. This happens when pmc is invoked with `GET` and `PARENT_DATA_SET` as two separate arguments instead of a single quoted string `"GET PARENT_DATA_SET"`. The newly introduced `RunPMCGetParentDS` function in `pkg/pmc/pmc.go` (line 294) does pass them as one arg (`exec.Command("pmc", ..., cmdStr)` where `cmdStr = "GET PARENT_DATA_SET"`), but some calling path in the conformance-test binary from `k8snetworkplumbingwg/ptp-operator@main` is splitting this into two separate argv entries.   - **Suggested Fix:** Find where the conformance-test binary (in `k8snetworkplumbingwg/ptp-operator` or via an imported daemon library function) calls `exec.Command("pmc", ..., "GET", "PARENT_DATA_SET")` and change it to pass the command as a single arg: `exec.Command("pmc", ..., "GET PARENT_DATA_SET")`.     Expected <int>: 248 to equal <int>: 6

    Expected ptp4l clock class to eventually be 6 for GM
    Expected <bool>: false to be true

## tgm

### Suite: tgm (11 failures)

**Suite TL;DR:** The WPC T-GM node never achieves LOCKED state (ptp4l clock class stays at 248) despite DPLL hardware being LOCKED, causing all GM-dependent tests to fail via timeouts or stale FREERUN metrics, with one additional separate regression resetting the ts2phc restart counter on PtpConfig re-apply.

---

**Root Cause Groups:**

- **Group 1: WPC T-GM servo never reaches LOCKED — cascading failure** (affects: Should check for ptp events; Should recover clockClass via event API after cloud-event-proxy crash; Should receive events after linuxptp-daemon pod restart; Should restart phc2sys with no socket errors after SIGTERM; is verifying WPC GM state based on logs; is verifying WPC GM state based on metrics; Verify ts2phc clock state is not LOCKED after GM PtpConfig is deleted; Testing WPC T-GM holdover through connection loss; Continuously terminating ts2phc triggers FREERUN event and then recovers to LOCKED; Testing T-GM Events on GNSS reboot and recovery)

  - **Evidence:**
    ```
    openshift_ptp_clock_state{iface="ens7fx",node="cnfdf32...",process="dpll"}   1
    openshift_ptp_clock_state{iface="ens7fx",node="cnfdf32...",process="ts2phc"} 0
    ```
    ```
    Expected ptp4l clock class to eventually be 6 for GM
    Expected <bool>: false  to be true
    ```
    ```
    could not find regex in log stream for openshift-ptp/linuxptp-daemon-g64pn
      container=linuxptp-daemon-container, err=error reading from stream: context deadline exceeded
    ```
    ```
    Expected phc2sys process status to be 1 for GM
    Expected <string>: 0  to equal  <string>: 1
    ```

  - **Root Cause:** The DPLL hardware on `cnfdf32` is LOCKED (`dpll=1`) confirming GNSS signal is valid and 1PPS is present, but ts2phc software servo remains in FREERUN (`ts2phc=0`). This mismatch indicates a software regression in the linuxptp-daemon: ts2phc's servo state is not advancing past `s0/s1` to `s2`. Because ts2phc never reports LOCKED, `HandleDelayedPhc2sysStartup` in `daemon.go:1290-1294` never fires, so phc2sys startup stays suppressed (process_status=0). With ts2phc in FREERUN, ptp4l's clock class stays at 248 (GM not traceable), no CloudEvent LOCKED events are emitted, and all log-stream tests hit context deadline waiting for patterns that never appear. The most likely cause is a regression introduced by `k8snetworkplumbingwg/linuxptp-daemon` PR #629 "Sync from upstream (22-Jul-2026)" (HEAD `14eb788`), which is the only recent change to that codebase. This sync may have altered ts2phc log parsing regex/state machine or GM clock-class propagation logic (`processParsedMetrics`, `log_parsing.go:82–153`; `ProcessTs2PhcEvents`, `daemon.go:2134–2190`). The `cloud-event-proxy` PR #722 (Jul 27, `0a69e46`) which widens PTP thresholds for ntpfailover profiles is a less likely cause since the WPC T-GM profile does not use the `ntpfailover` plugin and the `isNtpFailoverEnabled()` guard in `config.go:338–350` would return false.

  - **Breaking PR/Commit:** `k8snetworkplumbingwg/linuxptp-daemon` PR [#629](https://github.com/k8snetworkplumbingwg/linuxptp-daemon/pull/629) "Sync from upstream (22-Jul-2026)" — HEAD `14eb788`. (Job uses `USE_UPSTREAM=true` and clones this repo's `main` branch directly; branch-awareness check for `release-5.0` does not apply to this upstream component.)

  - **Is it a flake?** No — all 10 affected tests show the same deterministic "GM never LOCKED" pattern with hardware DPLL confirmed LOCKED; this is a consistent functional regression, not a timing issue.

  - **Suggested Fix:** Bisect `k8snetworkplumbingwg/linuxptp-daemon` main against the previous commit before `14eb788` to confirm the regression; specifically review changes to `pkg/parser/ts2phc_parser.go`, `pkg/daemon/log_parsing.go:processParsedMetrics`, and `pkg/daemon/daemon.go:ProcessTs2PhcEvents` for any change that could prevent `s2` servo state from being recognized as LOCKED or prevent the ts2phc LOCKED event from being forwarded to the GM state machine.

---

- **Group 2: ts2phc `ProcessRestartCount` metric reset on PtpConfig re-apply** (affects: Verify ts2phc metrics are cleaned up after GM PtpConfig delete and re-apply)

  - **Evidence:**
    ```
    ts2phc restart count should continue after re-apply (not reset), got 4 (initial was 7)
    Expected <int>: 4  to be >=  <int>: 7
    ```
    In `linuxptp-daemon/pkg/daemon/metrics.go:651–656`:
    ```go
    func deleteProcessStatusMetrics(config, process string) {
        ProcessStatus.Delete(...)
        ProcessRestartCount.Delete(...)   // ← counter is deleted here
    }
    ```
    In `metrics.go:556–562`:
    ```go
    func UpdateProcessStatusMetrics(process, cfgName string, status int64) {
        ProcessStatus.With(...).Set(float64(status))
        if status == PtpProcessUp {
            ProcessRestartCount.With(...).Inc()   // restarts from 0 after delete
        }
    }
    ```

  - **Root Cause:** When the GM PtpConfig is deleted, `deleteProcessStatusMetrics` (called from `deleteMetrics`, `metrics.go:610–649`) removes the `ProcessRestartCount` counter label entirely. After PtpConfig re-apply, ts2phc restarts from 0 and accumulates only 4 new restarts, which is less than the original 7. The test expectation is that the counter persists (monotonically increases) across delete/re-apply, but the `Delete()` call at `metrics.go:654` resets it. This is a separate logic bug from the GM LOCKED failure above, likely introduced by the same linuxptp-daemon `14eb788` upstream sync if it added the `ProcessRestartCount.Delete` call; if that line predates this run, the test itself may be newly tightened.

  - **Breaking PR/Commit:** Same linuxptp-daemon PR `14eb788` / `k8snetworkplumbingwg/linuxptp-daemon` PR [#629](https://github.com/k8snetworkplumbingwg/linuxptp-daemon/pull/629) — Unknown whether `ProcessRestartCount.Delete` was added in that sync or predated it.

  - **Is it a flake?** No — deterministic: counter always resets to 0 on delete; 4 < 7 is a predictable arithmetic outcome of the current code path.

  - **Suggested Fix:** Remove the `ProcessRestartCount.Delete(...)` call from `deleteProcessStatusMetrics` in `linuxptp-daemon/pkg/daemon/metrics.go:654` so the counter persists across PtpConfig delete/re-apply, while still deleting `ProcessStatus` (a gauge) which should reset.

---

**Suite Severity:** CRITICAL

---

## Cross-Suite Summary — periodic-ci-openshift-release-main-nightly-5.0-e2e-telco5g-ptp-upstream

**Version:** 5.0 | **Total failures:** 36 | **Suites:** bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, tbc, all, tgm

**TL;DR:** Three independent `main`-branch regressions — a test key-scheme bug, a broken PMC invocation, and a T-BC topology mismatch — plus a ts2phc servo regression in the upstream sync caused all 36 failures.

---

## Root Cause Groups

- **2/36 failures — `createStoredEvent()` key-scheme change drops LOCKED state** (suites: bc, dualfollower)
  Commit `d20ffcbf` (PR #171, "CNF-19588") changed `test/pkg/event/event.go`'s `createStoredEvent()` to key the `StoredEventValues` map by `v.Resource` (ResourceAddress) instead of `v.DataType`. For `OsClockSyncState` events both the notification ("LOCKED") and metric ("-18") share the identical ResourceAddress, so the metric silently overwrites the notification in the loop. The test then reads `values["notification"]` and finds nothing, `wasLocked` is never set, and the test times out — even though the production cloud-event-proxy correctly delivered LOCKED.

- **21/36 failures — PMC command split + BC/HA clock stuck at FREERUN (clock class 248)** (suites: dualnicbc, dualnicbcha)
  Commit `14eb788` (PR #629, "Sync from upstream 22-Jul-2026" in `k8snetworkplumbingwg/linuxptp-daemon`) introduced a behavioral regression where pmc receives `GET` and `PARENT_DATA_SET` as two separate argv tokens instead of a single quoted string, returning `bad command: GET` / `bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET` for every PMC call. This prevents the test from reading `parentPortIdentity` or `grandmasterIdentity`, causing role-assertion failures (`ens2f0np0` stays in MASTER instead of SLAVE) and preventing clock class from ever reaching 6. All downstream clock-sync, outage-recovery, event-API, and metrics tests cascade from this single invocation bug.

- **2/36 failures — T-BC topology solver returns zero solutions** (suites: tbc, all)
  Commit `84723c83` (PR #205, "test: Add T-BC CI tests and configuration") added `PtpConfigTelcoBC()` and its `AlgoTelcoBCString="TBC"` constraint set to `test/pkg/testconfig/testconfig.go`, requiring a WPC NIC with receiver + two same-NIC transmitter ports and a co-located WPC GM. The CI cluster (`cnfdf30`–`cnfdf32`) does not have this physical topology — only `cnfdf32` has WPC hardware (confirmed as the TGM node). `SynchronizedBeforeSuite` calls `CreatePtpConfigurationsWithRetry(3)`, the solver returns empty, and the suite is torn down before any test runs.

- **11/36 failures — WPC T-GM ts2phc servo stuck in FREERUN despite DPLL LOCKED** (suite: tgm)
  Also attributable to commit `14eb788` (PR #629 upstream sync). DPLL hardware on `cnfdf32` reports LOCKED (`dpll=1`) confirming valid GNSS/1PPS, but ts2phc software servo stays at FREERUN (`ts2phc=0`), indicating a regression in ts2phc log parsing, servo state-machine advancement, or GM clock-class propagation introduced by the sync (`log_parsing.go:82–153`, `ProcessTs2PhcEvents` in `daemon.go:2134–2190`). With ts2phc in FREERUN, `HandleDelayedPhc2sysStartup` never fires, phc2sys stays down (process_status=0), ptp4l clock class stays at 248, no CloudEvent LOCKED events are emitted, and all log-stream tests hit context deadline.

---

---

## Actionable Recommendations

1. **Revert or fix `14eb788` (PR #629 upstream sync) in `k8snetworkplumbingwg/linuxptp-daemon`** — This single commit accounts for 32/36 failures across dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, and tgm. ### Suite: bc (1 failures)

**Suite TL;DR:** The single bc-parallel failure is caused by a test-code regression in `createStoredEvent()` that changed the StoredEventValues map key from `v.DataType` ("notification"/"metric") to `v.Resource` (full ResourceAddress), silently dropping the LOCKED state so the test can never observe it.

**Root Cause Groups:**

- **Group 1: Test code key-scheme change in `createStoredEvent()` silently hides LOCKED state** (affects: `[It] [bc-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync`)
  - **Evidence:**
    ```
    [ptp.go: 411] got map[eventsource:/sync/sync-status/os-clock-sync-state
      eventtimestamp:2026-07-29 09:44:07.684026654 +0000 UTC
      eventtype:event.sync.sync-status.os-clock-sync-state-change
      eventvalues:map[/cluster/node/cnfdf30.telco5gran.eng.rdu2.redhat.com/CLOCK_REALTIME:-18]]
    [ptp.go: 419] clockOffset=0.000000
    [FAILED] OS Clock was never LOCKED and test timed out
    In [It] at: /tmp/cnf-pDNPW/ptp-operator-conformance-test/test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:393
    ```
    The raw cloud event data (logged by `event.go: 730`) clearly shows:
    ```json
    {"values":[
      {"ResourceAddress":"...CLOCK_REALTIME","data_type":"notification","value_type":"enumeration","value":"LOCKED"},
      {"ResourceAddress":"...CLOCK_REALTIME","data_type":"metric","value_type":"decimal64.3","value":"-18"}
    ]}
    ```
    The LOCKED event was delivered, but `values["notification"]` and `values["metric"]` were both `nil` in the test.

  - **Root Cause:** Commit `d20ffcbf` (PR #171, `CNF-19588`) changed `createStoredEvent()` in `test/pkg/event/event.go` (v1 path lines 711–717, v2 path lines 742–751) from using `v.DataType` as the map key to using `v.Resource` (the ResourceAddress). For `OsClockSyncState` events the notification value and metric value **share the same ResourceAddress** (`/cluster/node/.../CLOCK_REALTIME`), so the metric entry (`-18`) overwrites the notification entry (`LOCKED`) in the loop. The test at `ptp.go:414-415` then reads `values["notification"]` and `values["metric"]` — both return nil because those keys no longer exist — so `state` is `""` instead of `"LOCKED"`, `wasLocked` is never set `true`, and the test times out at `ptp.go:393`.

  - **Breaking PR/Commit:** Commit `d20ffcbf0cecd1cf94987788c703fa8d4565ba4d` — "CNF-19588: CI test for clockClass recovery after cloud-event-proxy crash" (merged as [PR #171](https://github.com/k8snetworkplumbingwg/ptp-operator/pull/171) on `main`). This is a `main`-only test code change; the `release-5.0` production images are unaffected. The OS clock on the hardware IS reaching LOCKED — the cloud event confirms it — but the test framework can't see it.

  - **Is it a flake?** No — the bug is deterministic. Every run will fail to observe LOCKED until the test times out.

  - **Suggested Fix:** In `test/pkg/event/event.go`'s `createStoredEvent()`, use a composite key `<ResourceAddress>:<DataType>` (or fall back to `DataType` when ResourceAddress is empty), so that OsClockSyncState events retain distinct "notification" and "metric" entries while BC clock class events with multiple "metric" values on different resources still don't collide. Alternatively, update `ptp.go:414-415` to iterate the values map and match by DataType rather than by fixed string keys.

**Suite Issue Class:** test_regression
**Suite Severity:** HIGH

## tbc

### Suite: tbc (1 failures)

**Suite TL;DR:** The `SynchronizedBeforeSuite` for the tbc-serial suite fails immediately because the L2-topology solver finds zero valid T-BC hardware configurations on the CI cluster, which in turn marks the single tbc-serial test as failed before it can run.

**Root Cause Groups:**

- **Group 1: L2-topology solver finds no T-BC solution for the CI cluster hardware** (affects: `[It] [tbc-serial] PTP e2e tests PTP Reboot discovery The slave node is rebooted and discovered and in sync [Serial]`)
  - **Evidence:**
    ```
    # junit-failures.txt
    Test: [It] [tbc-serial] PTP e2e tests PTP Reboot discovery The slave node is rebooted and discovered and in sync [Serial]
      Message: Could not create a ptp config, err=no T-BC solution found for TBC

    Test: [SynchronizedBeforeSuite]
      Message: Could not create a ptp config
    Expected
        <*errors.errorString | 0xc0009383c0>:
        no T-BC solution found for TBC
    to be nil

    # ci-operator-build-log.txt
    + export TEST_BRANCH=main
    + TEST_BRANCH=main
    + export IMG_VERSION=release-5.0
    + IMG_VERSION=release-5.0
    ```
    The `SynchronizedBeforeSuite` (not the test itself) throws the error, so the whole tbc-serial suite is torn down immediately.

  - **Root Cause:** `PtpConfigTelcoBC()` in `test/pkg/testconfig/testconfig.go:1898-1899` returns `"no T-BC solution found for TBC"` when `len(*data.solutions[AlgoTelcoBCString]) == 0`. The T-BC solver (`AlgoTelcoBCString = "TBC"`) requires: (1) a WPC NIC as PTP receiver, (2) two transmitter ports on that *same* NIC, (3) a local grandmaster on the same LAN as the receiver, and (4) a second WPC NIC for the GM (steps defined at `testconfig.go:704-709`). The CI cluster (nodes `cnfdf30`/`cnfdf31`/`cnfdf32`) only has WPC-capable hardware on `cnfdf32` (the TGM node, confirmed by `iface="ens7fx",node="cnfdf32",process="ts2phc"` in tgm test output). No node satisfies the T-BC topology simultaneously. The tbc-serial test suite is **new**, added by commit `84723c83` (PR [#205](https://github.com/openshift/ptp-operator/pull/205), merged 2026-03-25), and ran for the first time on a cluster not provisioned for T-BC hardware.

  - **Breaking PR/Commit:** https://github.com/openshift/ptp-operator/pull/205 — commit `84723c83` (`test: Add T-BC CI tests and configuration`), merged main only. Tests run from `main` branch (`TEST_BRANCH=main`) so this code is active; images come from `release-5.0` (unrelated to this failure). The commit is not present on `release-5.0` (backport check script absent; only `main`-branch git log shows `aede1e93`/`84723c83`).

  - **Is it a flake?** No. The topology solver is deterministic; the cluster will always return zero T-BC solutions until a node with the required WPC NIC layout is provisioned.

  - **Suggested Fix:** Either (a) provision a CI cluster node with WPC NIC topology that satisfies the T-BC solver constraints (receiver + 2 transmitters on same NIC + GM on same LAN), or (b) add a `Skip()`/`GinkgoT().Skip()` guard in the `SynchronizedBeforeSuite` when `PtpConfigTelcoBC` returns `"no T-BC solution found"`, so the suite is gracefully skipped rather than fatally failed on clusters without T-BC hardware.

**Suite Issue Class:** test_regression
**Suite Severity:** MEDIUM

## tgm

---

### Suite: tgm (11 failures)

**Suite TL;DR:** The WPC T-GM node never achieves LOCKED state (ptp4l clock class stays at 248) despite DPLL hardware being LOCKED, causing all GM-dependent tests to fail via timeouts or stale FREERUN metrics, with one additional separate regression resetting the ts2phc restart counter on PtpConfig re-apply.

---

**Root Cause Groups:**

- **Group 1: WPC T-GM servo never reaches LOCKED — cascading failure** (affects: Should check for ptp events; Should recover clockClass via event API after cloud-event-proxy crash; Should receive events after linuxptp-daemon pod restart; Should restart phc2sys with no socket errors after SIGTERM; is verifying WPC GM state based on logs; is verifying WPC GM state based on metrics; Verify ts2phc clock state is not LOCKED after GM PtpConfig is deleted; Testing WPC T-GM holdover through connection loss; Continuously terminating ts2phc triggers FREERUN event and then recovers to LOCKED; Testing T-GM Events on GNSS reboot and recovery)

  - **Evidence:**
    ```
    openshift_ptp_clock_state{iface="ens7fx",node="cnfdf32...",process="dpll"}   1
    openshift_ptp_clock_state{iface="ens7fx",node="cnfdf32...",process="ts2phc"} 0
    ```
    ```
    Expected ptp4l clock class to eventually be 6 for GM
    Expected <bool>: false  to be true
    ```
    ```
    could not find regex in log stream for openshift-ptp/linuxptp-daemon-g64pn
      container=linuxptp-daemon-container, err=error reading from stream: context deadline exceeded
    ```
    ```
    Expected phc2sys process status to be 1 for GM
    Expected <string>: 0  to equal  <string>: 1
    ```

  - **Root Cause:** The DPLL hardware on `cnfdf32` is LOCKED (`dpll=1`) confirming GNSS signal is valid and 1PPS is present, but ts2phc software servo remains in FREERUN (`ts2phc=0`). This mismatch indicates a software regression in the linuxptp-daemon: ts2phc's servo state is not advancing past `s0/s1` to `s2`. Because ts2phc never reports LOCKED, `HandleDelayedPhc2sysStartup` in `daemon.go:1290-1294` never fires, so phc2sys startup stays suppressed (process_status=0). With ts2phc in FREERUN, ptp4l's clock class stays at 248 (GM not traceable), no CloudEvent LOCKED events are emitted, and all log-stream tests hit context deadline waiting for patterns that never appear. The most likely cause is a regression introduced by `k8snetworkplumbingwg/linuxptp-daemon` PR #629 "Sync from upstream (22-Jul-2026)" (HEAD `14eb788`), which is the only recent change to that codebase. This sync may have altered ts2phc log parsing regex/state machine or GM clock-class propagation logic (`processParsedMetrics`, `log_parsing.go:82–153`; `ProcessTs2PhcEvents`, `daemon.go:2134–2190`). The `cloud-event-proxy` PR #722 (Jul 27, `0a69e46`) which widens PTP thresholds for ntpfailover profiles is a less likely cause since the WPC T-GM profile does not use the `ntpfailover` plugin and the `isNtpFailoverEnabled()` guard in `config.go:338–350` would return false.

  - **Breaking PR/Commit:** `k8snetworkplumbingwg/linuxptp-daemon` PR [#629](https://github.com/k8snetworkplumbingwg/linuxptp-daemon/pull/629) "Sync from upstream (22-Jul-2026)" — HEAD `14eb788`. (Job uses `USE_UPSTREAM=true` and clones this repo's `main` branch directly; branch-awareness check for `release-5.0` does not apply to this upstream component.)

  - **Is it a flake?** No — all 10 affected tests show the same deterministic "GM never LOCKED" pattern with hardware DPLL confirmed LOCKED; this is a consistent functional regression, not a timing issue.

  - **Suggested Fix:** Bisect `k8snetworkplumbingwg/linuxptp-daemon` main against the previous commit before `14eb788` to confirm the regression; specifically review changes to `pkg/parser/ts2phc_parser.go`, `pkg/daemon/log_parsing.go:processParsedMetrics`, and `pkg/daemon/daemon.go:ProcessTs2PhcEvents` for any change that could prevent `s2` servo state from being recognized as LOCKED or prevent the ts2phc LOCKED event from being forwarded to the GM state machine.

---

- **Group 2: ts2phc `ProcessRestartCount` metric reset on PtpConfig re-apply** (affects: Verify ts2phc metrics are cleaned up after GM PtpConfig delete and re-apply)

  - **Evidence:**
    ```
    ts2phc restart count should continue after re-apply (not reset), got 4 (initial was 7)
    Expected <int>: 4  to be >=  <int>: 7
    ```
    In `linuxptp-daemon/pkg/daemon/metrics.go:651–656`:
    ```go
    func deleteProcessStatusMetrics(config, process string) {
        ProcessStatus.Delete(...)
        ProcessRestartCount.Delete(...)   // ← counter is deleted here
    }
    ```
    In `metrics.go:556–562`:
    ```go
    func UpdateProcessStatusMetrics(process, cfgName string, status int64) {
        ProcessStatus.With(...).Set(float64(status))
        if status == PtpProcessUp {
            ProcessRestartCount.With(...).Inc()   // restarts from 0 after delete
        }
    }
    ```

  - **Root Cause:** When the GM PtpConfig is deleted, `deleteProcessStatusMetrics` (called from `deleteMetrics`, `metrics.go:610–649`) removes the `ProcessRestartCount` counter label entirely. After PtpConfig re-apply, ts2phc restarts from 0 and accumulates only 4 new restarts, which is less than the original 7. The test expectation is that the counter persists (monotonically increases) across delete/re-apply, but the `Delete()` call at `metrics.go:654` resets it. This is a separate logic bug from the GM LOCKED failure above, likely introduced by the same linuxptp-daemon `14eb788` upstream sync if it added the `ProcessRestartCount.Delete` call; if that line predates this run, the test itself may be newly tightened.

  - **Breaking PR/Commit:** Same linuxptp-daemon PR `14eb788` / `k8snetworkplumbingwg/linuxptp-daemon` PR [#629](https://github.com/k8snetworkplumbingwg/linuxptp-daemon/pull/629) — Unknown whether `ProcessRestartCount.Delete` was added in that sync or predated it.

  - **Is it a flake?** No — deterministic: counter always resets to 0 on delete; 4 < 7 is a predictable arithmetic outcome of the current code path.

  - **Suggested Fix:** Remove the `ProcessRestartCount.Delete(...)` call from `deleteProcessStatusMetrics` in `linuxptp-daemon/pkg/daemon/metrics.go:654` so the counter persists across PtpConfig delete/re-apply, while still deleting `ProcessStatus` (a gauge) which should reset.

---

**Suite Issue Class:** test_regression
**Suite Severity:** CRITICAL

---

## Cross-Suite Summary — periodic-ci-openshift-release-main-nightly-5.0-e2e-telco5g-ptp-upstream

**Version:** 5.0 | **Total failures:** 36 | **Suites:** bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, tbc, all, tgm

**TL;DR:** Three independent `main`-branch regressions — a test key-scheme bug, a broken PMC invocation, and a T-BC topology mismatch — plus a ts2phc servo regression in the upstream sync caused all 36 failures.

---

## Root Cause Groups

- **2/36 failures — `createStoredEvent()` key-scheme change drops LOCKED state** (suites: bc, dualfollower)
  Commit `d20ffcbf` (PR #171, "CNF-19588") changed `test/pkg/event/event.go`'s `createStoredEvent()` to key the `StoredEventValues` map by `v.Resource` (ResourceAddress) instead of `v.DataType`. For `OsClockSyncState` events both the notification ("LOCKED") and metric ("-18") share the identical ResourceAddress, so the metric silently overwrites the notification in the loop. The test then reads `values["notification"]` and finds nothing, `wasLocked` is never set, and the test times out — even though the production cloud-event-proxy correctly delivered LOCKED.

- **21/36 failures — PMC command split + BC/HA clock stuck at FREERUN (clock class 248)** (suites: dualnicbc, dualnicbcha)
  Commit `14eb788` (PR #629, "Sync from upstream 22-Jul-2026" in `k8snetworkplumbingwg/linuxptp-daemon`) introduced a behavioral regression where pmc receives `GET` and `PARENT_DATA_SET` as two separate argv tokens instead of a single quoted string, returning `bad command: GET` / `bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET` for every PMC call. This prevents the test from reading `parentPortIdentity` or `grandmasterIdentity`, causing role-assertion failures (`ens2f0np0` stays in MASTER instead of SLAVE) and preventing clock class from ever reaching 6. All downstream clock-sync, outage-recovery, event-API, and metrics tests cascade from this single invocation bug.

- **2/36 failures — T-BC topology solver returns zero solutions** (suites: tbc, all)
  Commit `84723c83` (PR #205, "test: Add T-BC CI tests and configuration") added `PtpConfigTelcoBC()` and its `AlgoTelcoBCString="TBC"` constraint set to `test/pkg/testconfig/testconfig.go`, requiring a WPC NIC with receiver + two same-NIC transmitter ports and a co-located WPC GM. The CI cluster (`cnfdf30`–`cnfdf32`) does not have this physical topology — only `cnfdf32` has WPC hardware (confirmed as the TGM node). `SynchronizedBeforeSuite` calls `CreatePtpConfigurationsWithRetry(3)`, the solver returns empty, and the suite is torn down before any test runs.

- **11/36 failures — WPC T-GM ts2phc servo stuck in FREERUN despite DPLL LOCKED** (suite: tgm)
  Also attributable to commit `14eb788` (PR #629 upstream sync). DPLL hardware on `cnfdf32` reports LOCKED (`dpll=1`) confirming valid GNSS/1PPS, but ts2phc software servo stays at FREERUN (`ts2phc=0`), indicating a regression in ts2phc log parsing, servo state-machine advancement, or GM clock-class propagation introduced by the sync (`log_parsing.go:82–153`, `ProcessTs2PhcEvents` in `daemon.go:2134–2190`). With ts2phc in FREERUN, `HandleDelayedPhc2sysStartup` never fires, phc2sys stays down (process_status=0), ptp4l clock class stays at 248, no CloudEvent LOCKED events are emitted, and all log-stream tests hit context deadline.

---

## Cross-Suite Patterns

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `createStoredEvent()` key-scheme drops LOCKED | ✓ | ✓ | — | — | — | — | — | No (2 suites) |
| PMC split-arg + BC stuck FREERUN (PR #629) | — | — | ✓ | ✓ | — | — | — | No (2 suites) |
| T-BC topology solver no solution (PR #205) | — | — | — | — | ✓ | ✓ | — | No (2 suites) |
| ts2phc servo FREERUN despite DPLL LOCKED (PR #629) | — | — | — | — | — | — | ✓ | Yes (1 suite) |

---

## Actionable Recommendations

1. **Revert or fix `14eb788` (PR #629 upstream sync) in `k8snetworkplumbingwg/linuxptp-daemon`** — This single commit accounts for 32/36 failures across dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, and tgm. Fix the PMC invocation so `GET PARENT_DATA_SET` is passed as a single argv token (not split), and investigate the ts2phc servo state-machine regression to restore LOCKED propagation from DPLL to ts2phc. Until fixed, block this image from nightly jobs or pin to the pre-`14eb788` image.

2. **Fix `createStoredEvent()` key collision in `test/pkg/event/event.go`** (commit `d20ffcbf`, PR #171) — Change the `StoredEventValues` map key from `v.Resource` alone to a composite `<ResourceAddress>:<DataType>` (or revert to `v.DataType`). This eliminates the 2 bc/dualfollower failures immediately with a one-line change. Add a unit test asserting that a `CLOCK_REALTIME` event with both a notification and a metric entry produces two distinct map entries.

3. **Add a `Skip()` guard in the T-BC suite setup** (commit `84723c83`, PR #205) — In `PtpConfigTelcoBC()` or the T-BC `SynchronizedBeforeSuite`, replace the hard `Expect(err).To(BeNil())` with a `Skip()` when the topology solver returns no solution. This prevents 2 suite-level failures and unblocks CI reporting for the rest of the job. Separately, work with the lab team to provision a WPC node satisfying the T-BC constraint (receiver + ≥2 same-NIC transmitters + co-located WPC GM) so the test can eventually run end-to-end.

### Suite: bc (1 failures)

**Suite TL;DR:** The single bc-parallel failure is caused by a test-code regression in `createStoredEvent()` that changed the StoredEventValues map key from `v.DataType` ("notification"/"metric") to `v.Resource` (full ResourceAddress), silently dropping the LOCKED state so the test can never observe it.

**Root Cause Groups:**

- **Group 1: Test code key-scheme change in `createStoredEvent()` silently hides LOCKED state** (affects: `[It] [bc-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync`)
  - **Evidence:**
    ```
    [ptp.go: 411] got map[eventsource:/sync/sync-status/os-clock-sync-state
      eventtimestamp:2026-07-29 09:44:07.684026654 +0000 UTC
      eventtype:event.sync.sync-status.os-clock-sync-state-change
      eventvalues:map[/cluster/node/cnfdf30.telco5gran.eng.rdu2.redhat.com/CLOCK_REALTIME:-18]]
    [ptp.go: 419] clockOffset=0.000000
    [FAILED] OS Clock was never LOCKED and test timed out
    In [It] at: /tmp/cnf-pDNPW/ptp-operator-conformance-test/test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:393
    ```
    The raw cloud event data (logged by `event.go: 730`) clearly shows:
    ```json
    {"values":[
      {"ResourceAddress":"...CLOCK_REALTIME","data_type":"notification","value_type":"enumeration","value":"LOCKED"},
      {"ResourceAddress":"...CLOCK_REALTIME","data_type":"metric","value_type":"decimal64.3","value":"-18"}
    ]}
    ```
    The LOCKED event was delivered, but `values["notification"]` and `values["metric"]` were both `nil` in the test.

  - **Root Cause:** Commit `d20ffcbf` (PR #171, `CNF-19588`) changed `createStoredEvent()` in `test/pkg/event/event.go` (v1 path lines 711–717, v2 path lines 742–751) from using `v.DataType` as the map key to using `v.Resource` (the ResourceAddress). For `OsClockSyncState` events the notification value and metric value **share the same ResourceAddress** (`/cluster/node/.../CLOCK_REALTIME`), so the metric entry (`-18`) overwrites the notification entry (`LOCKED`) in the loop. The test at `ptp.go:414-415` then reads `values["notification"]` and `values["metric"]` — both return nil because those keys no longer exist — so `state` is `""` instead of `"LOCKED"`, `wasLocked` is never set `true`, and the test times out at `ptp.go:393`.

  - **Breaking PR/Commit:** Commit `d20ffcbf0cecd1cf94987788c703fa8d4565ba4d` — "CNF-19588: CI test for clockClass recovery after cloud-event-proxy crash" (merged as [PR #171](https://github.com/k8snetworkplumbingwg/ptp-operator/pull/171) on `main`). This is a `main`-only test code change; the `release-5.0` production images are unaffected. The OS clock on the hardware IS reaching LOCKED — the cloud event confirms it — but the test framework can't see it.

  - **Is it a flake?** No — the bug is deterministic. Every run will fail to observe LOCKED until the test times out.

  - **Suggested Fix:** In `test/pkg/event/event.go`'s `createStoredEvent()`, use a composite key `<ResourceAddress>:<DataType>` (or fall back to `DataType` when ResourceAddress is empty), so that OsClockSyncState events retain distinct "notification" and "metric" entries while BC clock class events with multiple "metric" values on different resources still don't collide. Alternatively, update `ptp.go:414-415` to iterate the values map and match by DataType rather than by fixed string keys.

**Suite Issue Class:** test_regression
**Suite Severity:** HIGH

## Cross-Suite Summary — periodic-ci-openshift-release-main-nightly-5.0-e2e-telco5g-ptp-upstream

**Version:** 5.0 | **Total failures:** 36 | **Suites:** bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, tbc, all, tgm

**TL;DR:** Three independent `main`-branch regressions — a test key-scheme bug, a broken PMC invocation, and a T-BC topology mismatch — plus a ts2phc servo regression in the upstream sync caused all 36 failures.

---

## Root Cause Groups

- **2/36 failures — `createStoredEvent()` key-scheme change drops LOCKED state** (suites: bc, dualfollower)
  Commit `d20ffcbf` (PR #171, "CNF-19588") changed `test/pkg/event/event.go`'s `createStoredEvent()` to key the `StoredEventValues` map by `v.Resource` (ResourceAddress) instead of `v.DataType`. For `OsClockSyncState` events both the notification ("LOCKED") and metric ("-18") share the identical ResourceAddress, so the metric silently overwrites the notification in the loop. The test then reads `values["notification"]` and finds nothing, `wasLocked` is never set, and the test times out — even though the production cloud-event-proxy correctly delivered LOCKED.

- **21/36 failures — PMC command split + BC/HA clock stuck at FREERUN (clock class 248)** (suites: dualnicbc, dualnicbcha)
  Commit `14eb788` (PR #629, "Sync from upstream 22-Jul-2026" in `k8snetworkplumbingwg/linuxptp-daemon`) introduced a behavioral regression where pmc receives `GET` and `PARENT_DATA_SET` as two separate argv tokens instead of a single quoted string, returning `bad command: GET` / `bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET` for every PMC call. This prevents the test from reading `parentPortIdentity` or `grandmasterIdentity`, causing role-assertion failures (`ens2f0np0` stays in MASTER instead of SLAVE) and preventing clock class from ever reaching 6. All downstream clock-sync, outage-recovery, event-API, and metrics tests cascade from this single invocation bug.

- **2/36 failures — T-BC topology solver returns zero solutions** (suites: tbc, all)
  Commit `84723c83` (PR #205, "test: Add T-BC CI tests and configuration") added `PtpConfigTelcoBC()` and its `AlgoTelcoBCString="TBC"` constraint set to `test/pkg/testconfig/testconfig.go`, requiring a WPC NIC with receiver + two same-NIC transmitter ports and a co-located WPC GM. The CI cluster (`cnfdf30`–`cnfdf32`) does not have this physical topology — only `cnfdf32` has WPC hardware (confirmed as the TGM node). `SynchronizedBeforeSuite` calls `CreatePtpConfigurationsWithRetry(3)`, the solver returns empty, and the suite is torn down before any test runs.

- **11/36 failures — WPC T-GM ts2phc servo stuck in FREERUN despite DPLL LOCKED** (suite: tgm)
  Also attributable to commit `14eb788` (PR #629 upstream sync). DPLL hardware on `cnfdf32` reports LOCKED (`dpll=1`) confirming valid GNSS/1PPS, but ts2phc software servo stays at FREERUN (`ts2phc=0`), indicating a regression in ts2phc log parsing, servo state-machine advancement, or GM clock-class propagation introduced by the sync (`log_parsing.go:82–153`, `ProcessTs2PhcEvents` in `daemon.go:2134–2190`). With ts2phc in FREERUN, `HandleDelayedPhc2sysStartup` never fires, phc2sys stays down (process_status=0), ptp4l clock class stays at 248, no CloudEvent LOCKED events are emitted, and all log-stream tests hit context deadline.

1. **Revert or fix `14eb788` (PR #629 upstream sync) in `k8snetworkplumbingwg/linuxptp-daemon`** — This single commit accounts for 32/36 failures across dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, and tgm. Fix the PMC invocation so `GET PARENT_DATA_SET` is passed as a single argv token (not split), and investigate the ts2phc servo state-machine regression to restore LOCKED propagation from DPLL to ts2phc. Until fixed, block this image from nightly jobs or pin to the pre-`14eb788` image.

2. **Fix `createStoredEvent()` key collision in `test/pkg/event/event.go`** (commit `d20ffcbf`, PR #171) — Change the `StoredEventValues` map key from `v.Resource` alone to a composite `<ResourceAddress>:<DataType>` (or revert to `v.DataType`). ### Suite: bc (1 failures)

**Suite TL;DR:** The single bc-parallel failure is caused by a test-code regression in `createStoredEvent()` that changed the StoredEventValues map key from `v.DataType` ("notification"/"metric") to `v.Resource` (full ResourceAddress), silently dropping the LOCKED state so the test can never observe it.

**Root Cause Groups:**

- **Group 1: Test code key-scheme change in `createStoredEvent()` silently hides LOCKED state** (affects: `[It] [bc-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync`)
  - **Evidence:**
    ```
    [ptp.go: 411] got map[eventsource:/sync/sync-status/os-clock-sync-state
      eventtimestamp:2026-07-29 09:44:07.684026654 +0000 UTC
      eventtype:event.sync.sync-status.os-clock-sync-state-change
      eventvalues:map[/cluster/node/cnfdf30.telco5gran.eng.rdu2.redhat.com/CLOCK_REALTIME:-18]]

    The raw cloud event data (logged by `event.go: 730`) clearly shows:
    ```json

      {"ResourceAddress":"...CLOCK_REALTIME","data_type":"notification","value_type":"enumeration","value":"LOCKED"},
      {"ResourceAddress":"...CLOCK_REALTIME","data_type":"metric","value_type":"decimal64.3","value":"-18"}
    ]}
    ```
    The LOCKED event was delivered, but `values["notification"]` and `values["metric"]` were both `nil` in the test.

  - **Root Cause:** Commit `d20ffcbf` (PR #171, `CNF-19588`) changed `createStoredEvent()` in `test/pkg/event/event.go` (v1 path lines 711–717, v2 path lines 742–751) from using `v.DataType` as the map key to using `v.Resource` (the ResourceAddress). For `OsClockSyncState` events the notification value and metric value **share the same ResourceAddress** (`/cluster/node/.../CLOCK_REALTIME`), so the metric entry (`-18`) overwrites the notification entry (`LOCKED`) in the loop. The test at `ptp.go:414-415` then reads `values["notification"]` and `values["metric"]` — both return nil because those keys no longer exist — so `state` is `""` instead of `"LOCKED"`, `wasLocked` is never set `true`, and the test times out at `ptp.go:393`.

This is a `main`-only test code change; the `release-5.0` production images are unaffected. The OS clock on the hardware IS reaching LOCKED — the cloud event confirms it — but the test framework can't see it.

  - **Is it a flake?** No — the bug is deterministic. Every run will fail to observe LOCKED until the test times out.

  - **Suggested Fix:** In `test/pkg/event/event.go`'s `createStoredEvent()`, use a composite key `<ResourceAddress>:<DataType>` (or fall back to `DataType` when ResourceAddress is empty), so that OsClockSyncState events retain distinct "notification" and "metric" entries while BC clock class events with multiple "metric" values on different resources still don't collide. Alternatively, update `ptp.go:414-415` to iterate the values map and match by DataType rather than by fixed string keys.

## Root Cause Groups

- **2/36 failures — `createStoredEvent()` key-scheme change drops LOCKED state** (suites: bc, dualfollower)
  Commit `d20ffcbf` (PR #171, "CNF-19588") changed `test/pkg/event/event.go`'s `createStoredEvent()` to key the `StoredEventValues` map by `v.Resource` (ResourceAddress) instead of `v.DataType`. For `OsClockSyncState` events both the notification ("LOCKED") and metric ("-18") share the identical ResourceAddress, so the metric silently overwrites the notification in the loop. The test then reads `values["notification"]` and finds nothing, `wasLocked` is never set, and the test times out — even though the production cloud-event-proxy correctly delivered LOCKED.

- **21/36 failures — PMC command split + BC/HA clock stuck at FREERUN (clock class 248)** (suites: dualnicbc, dualnicbcha)
  Commit `14eb788` (PR #629, "Sync from upstream 22-Jul-2026" in `k8snetworkplumbingwg/linuxptp-daemon`) introduced a behavioral regression where pmc receives `GET` and `PARENT_DATA_SET` as two separate argv tokens instead of a single quoted string, returning `bad command: GET` / `bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET` for every PMC call. This prevents the test from reading `parentPortIdentity` or `grandmasterIdentity`, causing role-assertion failures (`ens2f0np0` stays in MASTER instead of SLAVE) and preventing clock class from ever reaching 6.   Commit `84723c83` (PR #205, "test: Add T-BC CI tests and configuration") added `PtpConfigTelcoBC()` and its `AlgoTelcoBCString="TBC"` constraint set to `test/pkg/testconfig/testconfig.go`, requiring a WPC NIC with receiver + two same-NIC transmitter ports and a co-located WPC GM. **Suite TL;DR:** The single bc-parallel failure is caused by a test-code regression in `createStoredEvent()` that changed the StoredEventValues map key from `v.DataType` ("notification"/"metric") to `v.Resource` (full ResourceAddress), silently dropping the LOCKED state so the test can never observe it.

**Root Cause Groups:**

- **Group 1: Test code key-scheme change in `createStoredEvent()` silently hides LOCKED state** (affects: `[It] [bc-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync`)
  - **Evidence:**
    ```

      eventtimestamp:2026-07-29 09:44:07.684026654 +0000 UTC
      eventtype:event.sync.sync-status.os-clock-sync-state-change
      eventvalues:map[/cluster/node/cnfdf30.telco5gran.eng.rdu2.redhat.com/CLOCK_REALTIME:-18]]

    The raw cloud event data (logged by `event.go: 730`) clearly shows:

      {"ResourceAddress":"...CLOCK_REALTIME","data_type":"notification","value_type":"enumeration","value":"LOCKED"},
      {"ResourceAddress":"...CLOCK_REALTIME","data_type":"metric","value_type":"decimal64.3","value":"-18"}

    ```
    The LOCKED event was delivered, but `values["notification"]` and `values["metric"]` were both `nil` in the test.

  - **Root Cause:** Commit `d20ffcbf` (PR #171, `CNF-19588`) changed `createStoredEvent()` in `test/pkg/event/event.go` (v1 path lines 711–717, v2 path lines 742–751) from using `v.DataType` as the map key to using `v.Resource` (the ResourceAddress). For `OsClockSyncState` events the notification value and metric value **share the same ResourceAddress** (`/cluster/node/.../CLOCK_REALTIME`), so the metric entry (`-18`) overwrites the notification entry (`LOCKED`) in the loop. The test at `ptp.go:414-415` then reads `values["notification"]` and `values["metric"]` — both return nil because those keys no longer exist — so `state` is `""` instead of `"LOCKED"`, `wasLocked` is never set `true`, and the test times out at `ptp.go:393`.

**Suite TL;DR:** The dual-NIC boundary clock is stuck in FREERUN (clock class 248) and all PMC `GET PARENT_DATA_SET` queries return `bad command: GET / bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET`, cascading into clock-sync, event, outage-recovery, and metrics failures.

    bad command: GET
    bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET
    ```
  - **Root Cause:** linuxptp's `pmc` binary processes each remaining argv entry as a separate command (e.g., `do_command("GET")` then `do_command("PARENT_DATA_SET")`), producing one "bad command" error per token. This happens when pmc is invoked with `GET` and `PARENT_DATA_SET` as two separate arguments instead of a single quoted string `"GET PARENT_DATA_SET"`.   - **Suggested Fix:** Find where the conformance-test binary (in `k8snetworkplumbingwg/ptp-operator` or via an imported daemon library function) calls `exec.Command("pmc", ..., "GET", "PARENT_DATA_SET")` and change it to pass the command as a single arg: `exec.Command("pmc", ..., "GET PARENT_DATA_SET")`.     Expected <bool>: false to be true

### Suite: tgm (11 failures)

**Suite TL;DR:** The WPC T-GM node never achieves LOCKED state (ptp4l clock class stays at 248) despite DPLL hardware being LOCKED, causing all GM-dependent tests to fail via timeouts or stale FREERUN metrics, with one additional separate regression resetting the ts2phc restart counter on PtpConfig re-apply.

---

**Root Cause Groups:**

- **Group 1: WPC T-GM servo never reaches LOCKED — cascading failure** (affects: Should check for ptp events; Should recover clockClass via event API after cloud-event-proxy crash; Should receive events after linuxptp-daemon pod restart; Should restart phc2sys with no socket errors after SIGTERM; is verifying WPC GM state based on logs; is verifying WPC GM state based on metrics; Verify ts2phc clock state is not LOCKED after GM PtpConfig is deleted; Testing WPC T-GM holdover through connection loss; Continuously terminating ts2phc triggers FREERUN event and then recovers to LOCKED; Testing T-GM Events on GNSS reboot and recovery)

  - **Evidence:**
    ```
    openshift_ptp_clock_state{iface="ens7fx",node="cnfdf32...",process="dpll"}   1
    openshift_ptp_clock_state{iface="ens7fx",node="cnfdf32...",process="ts2phc"} 0
    ```
    ```
    Expected ptp4l clock class to eventually be 6 for GM
    Expected <bool>: false  to be true
    ```
    ```
    could not find regex in log stream for openshift-ptp/linuxptp-daemon-g64pn
      container=linuxptp-daemon-container, err=error reading from stream: context deadline exceeded
    ```
    ```
    Expected phc2sys process status to be 1 for GM
    Expected <string>: 0  to equal  <string>: 1
    ```

  - **Root Cause:** The DPLL hardware on `cnfdf32` is LOCKED (`dpll=1`) confirming GNSS signal is valid and 1PPS is present, but ts2phc software servo remains in FREERUN (`ts2phc=0`). This mismatch indicates a software regression in the linuxptp-daemon: ts2phc's servo state is not advancing past `s0/s1` to `s2`. Because ts2phc never reports LOCKED, `HandleDelayedPhc2sysStartup` in `daemon.go:1290-1294` never fires, so phc2sys startup stays suppressed (process_status=0). With ts2phc in FREERUN, ptp4l's clock class stays at 248 (GM not traceable), no CloudEvent LOCKED events are emitted, and all log-stream tests hit context deadline waiting for patterns that never appear. The most likely cause is a regression introduced by `k8snetworkplumbingwg/linuxptp-daemon` PR #629 "Sync from upstream (22-Jul-2026)" (HEAD `14eb788`), which is the only recent change to that codebase. This sync may have altered ts2phc log parsing regex/state machine or GM clock-class propagation logic (`processParsedMetrics`, `log_parsing.go:82–153`; `ProcessTs2PhcEvents`, `daemon.go:2134–2190`). The `cloud-event-proxy` PR #722 (Jul 27, `0a69e46`) which widens PTP thresholds for ntpfailover profiles is a less likely cause since the WPC T-GM profile does not use the `ntpfailover` plugin and the `isNtpFailoverEnabled()` guard in `config.go:338–350` would return false.

  - **Breaking PR/Commit:** `k8snetworkplumbingwg/linuxptp-daemon` PR [#629](https://github.com/k8snetworkplumbingwg/linuxptp-daemon/pull/629) "Sync from upstream (22-Jul-2026)" — HEAD `14eb788`. (Job uses `USE_UPSTREAM=true` and clones this repo's `main` branch directly; branch-awareness check for `release-5.0` does not apply to this upstream component.)

  - **Is it a flake?** No — all 10 affected tests show the same deterministic "GM never LOCKED" pattern with hardware DPLL confirmed LOCKED; this is a consistent functional regression, not a timing issue.

  - **Suggested Fix:** Bisect `k8snetworkplumbingwg/linuxptp-daemon` main against the previous commit before `14eb788` to confirm the regression; specifically review changes to `pkg/parser/ts2phc_parser.go`, `pkg/daemon/log_parsing.go:processParsedMetrics`, and `pkg/daemon/daemon.go:ProcessTs2PhcEvents` for any change that could prevent `s2` servo state from being recognized as LOCKED or prevent the ts2phc LOCKED event from being forwarded to the GM state machine.

---

- **Group 2: ts2phc `ProcessRestartCount` metric reset on PtpConfig re-apply** (affects: Verify ts2phc metrics are cleaned up after GM PtpConfig delete and re-apply)

  - **Evidence:**

    ts2phc restart count should continue after re-apply (not reset), got 4 (initial was 7)
    Expected <int>: 4  to be >=  <int>: 7
    ```
    In `linuxptp-daemon/pkg/daemon/metrics.go:651–656`:
    ```go
    func deleteProcessStatusMetrics(config, process string) {
        ProcessStatus.Delete(...)
        ProcessRestartCount.Delete(...)   // ← counter is deleted here
    }
    ```
    In `metrics.go:556–562`:
    ```go
    func UpdateProcessStatusMetrics(process, cfgName string, status int64) {
        ProcessStatus.With(...).Set(float64(status))
        if status == PtpProcessUp {
            ProcessRestartCount.With(...).Inc()   // restarts from 0 after delete
        }
    }
    ```

  - **Root Cause:** When the GM PtpConfig is deleted, `deleteProcessStatusMetrics` (called from `deleteMetrics`, `metrics.go:610–649`) removes the `ProcessRestartCount` counter label entirely. After PtpConfig re-apply, ts2phc restarts from 0 and accumulates only 4 new restarts, which is less than the original 7. The test expectation is that the counter persists (monotonically increases) across delete/re-apply, but the `Delete()` call at `metrics.go:654` resets it. This is a separate logic bug from the GM LOCKED failure above, likely introduced by the same linuxptp-daemon `14eb788` upstream sync if it added the `ProcessRestartCount.Delete` call; if that line predates this run, the test itself may be newly tightened.

  - **Is it a flake?** No — deterministic: counter always resets to 0 on delete; 4 < 7 is a predictable arithmetic outcome of the current code path.

  - **Suggested Fix:** Remove the `ProcessRestartCount.Delete(...)` call from `deleteProcessStatusMetrics` in `linuxptp-daemon/pkg/daemon/metrics.go:654` so the counter persists across PtpConfig delete/re-apply, while still deleting `ProcessStatus` (a gauge) which should reset.

## Cross-Suite Summary — periodic-ci-openshift-release-main-nightly-5.0-e2e-telco5g-ptp-upstream

**Version:** 5.0 | **Total failures:** 36 | **Suites:** bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, tbc, all, tgm

**TL;DR:** Three independent `main`-branch regressions — a test key-scheme bug, a broken PMC invocation, and a T-BC topology mismatch — plus a ts2phc servo regression in the upstream sync caused all 36 failures.

---

## Root Cause Groups

- **2/36 failures — `createStoredEvent()` key-scheme change drops LOCKED state** (suites: bc, dualfollower)
  Commit `d20ffcbf` (PR #171, "CNF-19588") changed `test/pkg/event/event.go`'s `createStoredEvent()` to key the `StoredEventValues` map by `v.Resource` (ResourceAddress) instead of `v.DataType`. For `OsClockSyncState` events both the notification ("LOCKED") and metric ("-18") share the identical ResourceAddress, so the metric silently overwrites the notification in the loop. The test then reads `values["notification"]` and finds nothing, `wasLocked` is never set, and the test times out — even though the production cloud-event-proxy correctly delivered LOCKED.

- **21/36 failures — PMC command split + BC/HA clock stuck at FREERUN (clock class 248)** (suites: dualnicbc, dualnicbcha)
  Commit `14eb788` (PR #629, "Sync from upstream 22-Jul-2026" in `k8snetworkplumbingwg/linuxptp-daemon`) introduced a behavioral regression where pmc receives `GET` and `PARENT_DATA_SET` as two separate argv tokens instead of a single quoted string, returning `bad command: GET` / `bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET` for every PMC call. This prevents the test from reading `parentPortIdentity` or `grandmasterIdentity`, causing role-assertion failures (`ens2f0np0` stays in MASTER instead of SLAVE) and preventing clock class from ever reaching 6. All downstream clock-sync, outage-recovery, event-API, and metrics tests cascade from this single invocation bug.

- **2/36 failures — T-BC topology solver returns zero solutions** (suites: tbc, all)
  Commit `84723c83` (PR #205, "test: Add T-BC CI tests and configuration") added `PtpConfigTelcoBC()` and its `AlgoTelcoBCString="TBC"` constraint set to `test/pkg/testconfig/testconfig.go`, requiring a WPC NIC with receiver + two same-NIC transmitter ports and a co-located WPC GM. The CI cluster (`cnfdf30`–`cnfdf32`) does not have this physical topology — only `cnfdf32` has WPC hardware (confirmed as the TGM node). `SynchronizedBeforeSuite` calls `CreatePtpConfigurationsWithRetry(3)`, the solver returns empty, and the suite is torn down before any test runs.

- **11/36 failures — WPC T-GM ts2phc servo stuck in FREERUN despite DPLL LOCKED** (suite: tgm)
  Also attributable to commit `14eb788` (PR #629 upstream sync). DPLL hardware on `cnfdf32` reports LOCKED (`dpll=1`) confirming valid GNSS/1PPS, but ts2phc software servo stays at FREERUN (`ts2phc=0`), indicating a regression in ts2phc log parsing, servo state-machine advancement, or GM clock-class propagation introduced by the sync (`log_parsing.go:82–153`, `ProcessTs2PhcEvents` in `daemon.go:2134–2190`). With ts2phc in FREERUN, `HandleDelayedPhc2sysStartup` never fires, phc2sys stays down (process_status=0), ptp4l clock class stays at 248, no CloudEvent LOCKED events are emitted, and all log-stream tests hit context deadline.

### Suite: bc (1 failures)

**Suite TL;DR:** The single bc-parallel failure is caused by a test-code regression in `createStoredEvent()` that changed the StoredEventValues map key from `v.DataType` ("notification"/"metric") to `v.Resource` (full ResourceAddress), silently dropping the LOCKED state so the test can never observe it.

**Root Cause Groups:**

- **Group 1: Test code key-scheme change in `createStoredEvent()` silently hides LOCKED state** (affects: `[It] [bc-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync`)
  - **Evidence:**
    ```
    [ptp.go: 411] got map[eventsource:/sync/sync-status/os-clock-sync-state
      eventtimestamp:2026-07-29 09:44:07.684026654 +0000 UTC
      eventtype:event.sync.sync-status.os-clock-sync-state-change
      eventvalues:map[/cluster/node/cnfdf30.telco5gran.eng.rdu2.redhat.com/CLOCK_REALTIME:-18]]
    [ptp.go: 419] clockOffset=0.000000
    [FAILED] OS Clock was never LOCKED and test timed out
    In [It] at: /tmp/cnf-pDNPW/ptp-operator-conformance-test/test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:393
    ```
    The raw cloud event data (logged by `event.go: 730`) clearly shows:
    ```json
    {"values":[
      {"ResourceAddress":"...CLOCK_REALTIME","data_type":"notification","value_type":"enumeration","value":"LOCKED"},
      {"ResourceAddress":"...CLOCK_REALTIME","data_type":"metric","value_type":"decimal64.3","value":"-18"}
    ]}
    ```
    The LOCKED event was delivered, but `values["notification"]` and `values["metric"]` were both `nil` in the test.

  - **Root Cause:** Commit `d20ffcbf` (PR #171, `CNF-19588`) changed `createStoredEvent()` in `test/pkg/event/event.go` (v1 path lines 711–717, v2 path lines 742–751) from using `v.DataType` as the map key to using `v.Resource` (the ResourceAddress). For `OsClockSyncState` events the notification value and metric value **share the same ResourceAddress** (`/cluster/node/.../CLOCK_REALTIME`), so the metric entry (`-18`) overwrites the notification entry (`LOCKED`) in the loop. The test at `ptp.go:414-415` then reads `values["notification"]` and `values["metric"]` — both return nil because those keys no longer exist — so `state` is `""` instead of `"LOCKED"`, `wasLocked` is never set `true`, and the test times out at `ptp.go:393`.

  - **Breaking PR/Commit:** Commit `d20ffcbf0cecd1cf94987788c703fa8d4565ba4d` — "CNF-19588: CI test for clockClass recovery after cloud-event-proxy crash" (merged as [PR #171](https://github.com/k8snetworkplumbingwg/ptp-operator/pull/171) on `main`). This is a `main`-only test code change; the `release-5.0` production images are unaffected. The OS clock on the hardware IS reaching LOCKED — the cloud event confirms it — but the test framework can't see it.

  - **Is it a flake?** No — the bug is deterministic. Every run will fail to observe LOCKED until the test times out.

  - **Suggested Fix:** In `test/pkg/event/event.go`'s `createStoredEvent()`, use a composite key `<ResourceAddress>:<DataType>` (or fall back to `DataType` when ResourceAddress is empty), so that OsClockSyncState events retain distinct "notification" and "metric" entries while BC clock class events with multiple "metric" values on different resources still don't collide. Alternatively, update `ptp.go:414-415` to iterate the values map and match by DataType rather than by fixed string keys.

**Suite Issue Class:** test_regression
**Suite Severity:** HIGH

The daemon's PMC invocation path is `pkg/pmc/pmc.go:RunPMCExpGetParentDS()` (spawns `pmc -u -b 0 -f /var/run/ptp4l.0.config` and sends `GET PARENT_DATA_SET\n`), which has not changed — but the ptp4l binary responding to it has. All 9 serial test failures are downstream cascades of this single ptp4l management breakage: without a valid PARENT_DATA_SET response, the test helper cannot determine clock identity; without SLAVE state, clock class never reaches 6; without clock class 6, phc2sys won't run; and all outage-recovery tests time out waiting for sync that never comes.
  - **Breaking PR/Commit:** `14eb788` — "Sync from upstream (22-Jul-2026)", https://github.com/k8snetworkplumbingwg/linuxptp-daemon/pull/629 (merged 2026-07-22). The `USE_UPSTREAM=true` flag in this job builds all three images directly from `main` branch, so this commit is live in the deployed image. The linuxptp RPM version bump (unpinned in Dockerfile, line 25: `linuxptp`) is the likely proximate trigger.
  - **Is it a flake?** No — the identical `bad command` pattern repeats across dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, bc, dualfollower, and tgm suites in the same run, and the interface role error (`MASTER` instead of `SLAVE`) is deterministic given no upstream GM lock. The failure mode is consistent and total.
  - **Suggested Fix:** Pin the `linuxptp` RPM to a known-good version in the Dockerfile (e.g., `linuxptp-3.1.1-*` or whichever version passed previously), or add a regression test that validates PMC `GET PARENT_DATA_SET` returns a parseable response before all other clock-sync tests run. Also investigate whether linuxptp 4.x changed the management domain or socket behavior and update `pmcCmdConstPart` in `pkg/pmc/pmc.go` accordingly if a version upgrade is intended.

- **Group 2: Event consumer log read timeout — context deadline exceeded** (affects: [dualnicbcha-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync)
  - **Evidence:**
    ```
    could not push initial event, err=error reading logs in ns=ptp-event-framework-test pod=consumer: context deadline exceeded
    ```
    The same pattern appears in dualnicbc-parallel and tgm-serial: `error reading logs in ns=ptp-event-framework-test pod=consumer: context deadline exceeded`.
  - **Root Cause:** The event consumer pod in `ptp-event-framework-test` namespace is not producing logs within the deadline. This is a likely cascade from the ptp4l sync failure (no PTP events are generated if ptp4l is in FREERUN), but could also be an independent issue with cloud-event-proxy's log streaming — cloud-event-proxy was also built from `redhat-cne/cloud-event-proxy@main` (latest commit `0a69e46`, "ntpThresholds" NTP PR). The test reads pod logs to detect initial events (`event.go:589` / `parallel_suite_test.go:117`) and the deadline is exceeded, suggesting the consumer pod never received any PTP state-change events to log.
  - **Breaking PR/Commit:** Unknown (may be cascade from Group 1; cloud-event-proxy `0a69e46` is an NTP-threshold change unrelated to PTP event streaming)
  - **Is it a flake?** No — consistent with the overall PTP sync failure; if no sync events are generated, the consumer will always time out.
  - **Suggested Fix:** After fixing the ptp4l management regression (Group 1), re-run to confirm this clears. If it persists, add a pre-check that verifies the consumer pod is Ready and cloud-event-proxy is subscribed before attempting the log-stream assertion.

**Suite Issue Class:** test_regression
**Suite Severity:** CRITICAL

### Suite: tbc (1 failures)

**Suite TL;DR:** The `SynchronizedBeforeSuite` for the tbc-serial suite fails immediately because the L2-topology solver finds zero valid T-BC hardware configurations on the CI cluster, which in turn marks the single tbc-serial test as failed before it can run.

**Root Cause Groups:**

- **Group 1: L2-topology solver finds no T-BC solution for the CI cluster hardware** (affects: `[It] [tbc-serial] PTP e2e tests PTP Reboot discovery The slave node is rebooted and discovered and in sync [Serial]`)
  - **Evidence:**
    ```

    Test: [It] [tbc-serial] PTP e2e tests PTP Reboot discovery The slave node is rebooted and discovered and in sync [Serial]
      Message: Could not create a ptp config, err=no T-BC solution found for TBC

    Test: [SynchronizedBeforeSuite]
      Message: Could not create a ptp config
    Expected
        <*errors.errorString | 0xc0009383c0>:

    + TEST_BRANCH=main
    + export IMG_VERSION=release-5.0
    + IMG_VERSION=release-5.0

The T-BC solver (`AlgoTelcoBCString = "TBC"`) requires: (1) a WPC NIC as PTP receiver, (2) two transmitter ports on that *same* NIC, (3) a local grandmaster on the same LAN as the receiver, and (4) a second WPC NIC for the GM (steps defined at `testconfig.go:704-709`). The CI cluster (nodes `cnfdf30`/`cnfdf31`/`cnfdf32`) only has WPC-capable hardware on `cnfdf32` (the TGM node, confirmed by `iface="ens7fx",node="cnfdf32",process="ts2phc"` in tgm test output). No node satisfies the T-BC topology simultaneously. The tbc-serial test suite is **new**, added by commit `84723c83` (PR [#205](https://github.com/openshift/ptp-operator/pull/205), merged 2026-03-25), and ran for the first time on a cluster not provisioned for T-BC hardware.

The commit is not present on `release-5.0` (backport check script absent; only `main`-branch git log shows `aede1e93`/`84723c83`).

  - **Suggested Fix:** Either (a) provision a CI cluster node with WPC NIC topology that satisfies the T-BC solver constraints (receiver + 2 transmitters on same NIC + GM on same LAN), or (b) add a `Skip()`/`GinkgoT().Skip()` guard in the `SynchronizedBeforeSuite` when `PtpConfigTelcoBC` returns `"no T-BC solution found"`, so the suite is gracefully skipped rather than fatally failed on clusters without T-BC hardware.

## tgm

---

### Suite: tgm (11 failures)

**Suite TL;DR:** The WPC T-GM node never achieves LOCKED state (ptp4l clock class stays at 248) despite DPLL hardware being LOCKED, causing all GM-dependent tests to fail via timeouts or stale FREERUN metrics, with one additional separate regression resetting the ts2phc restart counter on PtpConfig re-apply.

---

**Root Cause Groups:**

- **Group 1: WPC T-GM servo never reaches LOCKED — cascading failure** (affects: Should check for ptp events; Should recover clockClass via event API after cloud-event-proxy crash; Should receive events after linuxptp-daemon pod restart; Should restart phc2sys with no socket errors after SIGTERM; is verifying WPC GM state based on logs; is verifying WPC GM state based on metrics; Verify ts2phc clock state is not LOCKED after GM PtpConfig is deleted; Testing WPC T-GM holdover through connection loss; Continuously terminating ts2phc triggers FREERUN event and then recovers to LOCKED; Testing T-GM Events on GNSS reboot and recovery)

  - **Evidence:**
    ```
    openshift_ptp_clock_state{iface="ens7fx",node="cnfdf32...",process="dpll"}   1
    openshift_ptp_clock_state{iface="ens7fx",node="cnfdf32...",process="ts2phc"} 0
    ```
    ```
    Expected ptp4l clock class to eventually be 6 for GM
    Expected <bool>: false  to be true
    ```
    ```
    could not find regex in log stream for openshift-ptp/linuxptp-daemon-g64pn
      container=linuxptp-daemon-container, err=error reading from stream: context deadline exceeded
    ```
    ```
    Expected phc2sys process status to be 1 for GM
    Expected <string>: 0  to equal  <string>: 1
    ```

  - **Root Cause:** The DPLL hardware on `cnfdf32` is LOCKED (`dpll=1`) confirming GNSS signal is valid and 1PPS is present, but ts2phc software servo remains in FREERUN (`ts2phc=0`). This mismatch indicates a software regression in the linuxptp-daemon: ts2phc's servo state is not advancing past `s0/s1` to `s2`. Because ts2phc never reports LOCKED, `HandleDelayedPhc2sysStartup` in `daemon.go:1290-1294` never fires, so phc2sys startup stays suppressed (process_status=0). With ts2phc in FREERUN, ptp4l's clock class stays at 248 (GM not traceable), no CloudEvent LOCKED events are emitted, and all log-stream tests hit context deadline waiting for patterns that never appear. The most likely cause is a regression introduced by `k8snetworkplumbingwg/linuxptp-daemon` PR #629 "Sync from upstream (22-Jul-2026)" (HEAD `14eb788`), which is the only recent change to that codebase. This sync may have altered ts2phc log parsing regex/state machine or GM clock-class propagation logic (`processParsedMetrics`, `log_parsing.go:82–153`; `ProcessTs2PhcEvents`, `daemon.go:2134–2190`). The `cloud-event-proxy` PR #722 (Jul 27, `0a69e46`) which widens PTP thresholds for ntpfailover profiles is a less likely cause since the WPC T-GM profile does not use the `ntpfailover` plugin and the `isNtpFailoverEnabled()` guard in `config.go:338–350` would return false.

  - **Breaking PR/Commit:** `k8snetworkplumbingwg/linuxptp-daemon` PR [#629](https://github.com/k8snetworkplumbingwg/linuxptp-daemon/pull/629) "Sync from upstream (22-Jul-2026)" — HEAD `14eb788`. (Job uses `USE_UPSTREAM=true` and clones this repo's `main` branch directly; branch-awareness check for `release-5.0` does not apply to this upstream component.)

  - **Is it a flake?** No — all 10 affected tests show the same deterministic "GM never LOCKED" pattern with hardware DPLL confirmed LOCKED; this is a consistent functional regression, not a timing issue.

  - **Suggested Fix:** Bisect `k8snetworkplumbingwg/linuxptp-daemon` main against the previous commit before `14eb788` to confirm the regression; specifically review changes to `pkg/parser/ts2phc_parser.go`, `pkg/daemon/log_parsing.go:processParsedMetrics`, and `pkg/daemon/daemon.go:ProcessTs2PhcEvents` for any change that could prevent `s2` servo state from being recognized as LOCKED or prevent the ts2phc LOCKED event from being forwarded to the GM state machine.

---

- **Group 2: ts2phc `ProcessRestartCount` metric reset on PtpConfig re-apply** (affects: Verify ts2phc metrics are cleaned up after GM PtpConfig delete and re-apply)

  - **Evidence:**
    ```
    ts2phc restart count should continue after re-apply (not reset), got 4 (initial was 7)
    Expected <int>: 4  to be >=  <int>: 7
    ```
    In `linuxptp-daemon/pkg/daemon/metrics.go:651–656`:
    ```go
    func deleteProcessStatusMetrics(config, process string) {
        ProcessStatus.Delete(...)
        ProcessRestartCount.Delete(...)   // ← counter is deleted here
    }
    ```
    In `metrics.go:556–562`:
    ```go
    func UpdateProcessStatusMetrics(process, cfgName string, status int64) {
        ProcessStatus.With(...).Set(float64(status))
        if status == PtpProcessUp {
            ProcessRestartCount.With(...).Inc()   // restarts from 0 after delete
        }
    }
    ```

  - **Root Cause:** When the GM PtpConfig is deleted, `deleteProcessStatusMetrics` (called from `deleteMetrics`, `metrics.go:610–649`) removes the `ProcessRestartCount` counter label entirely. After PtpConfig re-apply, ts2phc restarts from 0 and accumulates only 4 new restarts, which is less than the original 7. The test expectation is that the counter persists (monotonically increases) across delete/re-apply, but the `Delete()` call at `metrics.go:654` resets it. This is a separate logic bug from the GM LOCKED failure above, likely introduced by the same linuxptp-daemon `14eb788` upstream sync if it added the `ProcessRestartCount.Delete` call; if that line predates this run, the test itself may be newly tightened.

  - **Breaking PR/Commit:** Same linuxptp-daemon PR `14eb788` / `k8snetworkplumbingwg/linuxptp-daemon` PR [#629](https://github.com/k8snetworkplumbingwg/linuxptp-daemon/pull/629) — Unknown whether `ProcessRestartCount.Delete` was added in that sync or predated it.

  - **Is it a flake?** No — deterministic: counter always resets to 0 on delete; 4 < 7 is a predictable arithmetic outcome of the current code path.

  - **Suggested Fix:** Remove the `ProcessRestartCount.Delete(...)` call from `deleteProcessStatusMetrics` in `linuxptp-daemon/pkg/daemon/metrics.go:654` so the counter persists across PtpConfig delete/re-apply, while still deleting `ProcessStatus` (a gauge) which should reset.
